reference.title: Dumbbell JM Bench Press
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Upper Arms, equipment Dumbbell, exercise type Strength
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Inhale as the dumbbells come down toward the upper chest, exhale as you press.
breathing.cadence: About 2.0 s down, 0.3 s pause, 1.2 s up

prescription.load: Dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can lift for the target reps with 1-3 reps in reserve (RIR 1-3, about RPE 7-9).
prescription.progression: More reps, then the next dumbbell; keep the elbow path the same.

cues.text: Lie on a flat bench, feet planted; dumbbells straight up over the shoulders, palms facing each other, elbows tucked.
Breathe in and let the elbows bend and drift down toward your feet together, bringing the dumbbells back toward the upper chest and chin.
Dumbbells just above the upper chest, forearms angled back, elbows pointing toward the feet; no contact with the face.
Breathe out and push the dumbbells straight back up, straightening the elbows.
Arms vertical over the shoulders; reset and repeat.

mistakes.mistake: Turning it into a regular press (elbows flaring out to the sides)
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbows tucked and pointing toward the feet.

mistakes.mistake: Turning it into a skull crusher (upper arms still)
mistakes.fix: Let the elbows travel down toward the feet as the forearms fold back; both joints move.
Lower under control to just above the upper chest.
Elbow-dominant pressing is hard on the elbows: progress slowly (clinical opinion).

kinematics.norm: From straight to deeply bent (about 110-130 degrees of flexion) at the bottom (clinical opinion; no measured norm found)
The upper arms tilt toward the feet as the elbows bend, about 40-55 degrees from vertical at the bottom (clinical opinion); the poster in Puluka reports less shoulder involvement than a regular press
Dumbbells travel back toward the upper chest and chin, not the face (clinical opinion)
Feet flat on the floor with the knees bent about 90 degrees, like the bench set-up in Solstad 2020 (head, shoulders and hips on the bench)
Controlled, about 2 s down and 1 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #1121312, Dumbbell JM Bench Press, video (movement reference)
Puluka, JM press vs skull crusher movement analysis (student biomechanics poster, Monmouth University; one male participant, surface EMG normalised to MVIC)

Saeterbakken, Stien, Pedersen, Solstad, Cumming and Andersen 2021, the effect of grip width on muscle strength and electromyographic activity in bench press among novice- and resistance-trained men (Int J Environ Res Public Health 18(12):6444; PMC8296276)
Boehler 2011, electromyographic analysis of the triceps brachii muscle during a variety of triceps exercises (MS thesis, University of Wisconsin-La Crosse)

cautions: Get into position safely: sit on the end of the bench with the dumbbells on the thighs, then lie back and kick them up one knee at a time; at the end of the set bring them back to the thighs or lower them to the floor beside the bench rather than dropping them (clinical opinion).
Elbow pain: the JM press loads the elbow heavily; reduce the depth or switch to a close-grip press (clinical opinion).
Lower to the upper chest, never to the face; stop the set if control is lost.
Keep the wrists straight over the forearms; bent-back wrists under a heavy dumbbell strain the wrist.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shorter range: stop when the dumbbells are a hand-width above the chest.
Lighter dumbbells while learning the elbow path.
regressions: Dumbbell skull crusher with light dumbbells.

muscleNotes.triceps_r: Main mover: a hybrid of a close-grip press and a lying extension, mostly elbow extension. In a one-person biomechanics poster the JM press gave higher triceps EMG than the skull crusher (0.65 vs 0.53 mV, Puluka); narrow-grip pressing also raises triceps activity (Saeterbakken 2021).
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Main mover: a hybrid of a close-grip press and a lying extension, mostly elbow extension. In a one-person biomechanics poster the JM press gave higher triceps EMG than the skull crusher (0.65 vs 0.53 mV, Puluka); narrow-grip pressing also raises triceps activity (Saeterbakken 2021).

muscleNotes.core: Bracing keeps the ribs down and the pelvis on the bench.
